questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes TypeScript access modifiers and JavaScript private fields?
options: TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
Both mechanisms are identical in all runtime behavior.
JavaScript #private fields are comments removed before execution.
questions.answer_key: TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
questions.explanation: Runtime behavior matters when selecting an encapsulation mechanism.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Access Modifiers”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with public and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with public and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “public”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Access Modifiers”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check private, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume protected is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check private, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “private”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
